name: Sechuran
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct, 'poorly attested Peruvian language of uncertain affiliation' (Glottolog); only colonial wordlists (Martinez Companon) discussed in Urban 2019 — no stress data possible.

sources.citation: Urban, Matthias. 2019. Lost Languages of the Peruvian North Coast. Estudios Indiana, 12. Berlin: Ibero-Amerikanisches Institut / Gebr. Mann Verlag. 314 pp. ISBN 978-3-7861-2826-7 (open access, IAI repository object iai_mods_00000019).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. V 'Sechura', section 'Sound system' pp. 104-108. p.104: Martinez Companon's (1782-90) Sechura list carries a grave accent on vowels (<tutù> 'water', <chùpchùp> 'star', <yòro> 'sun'); 'the significance of the grave remains unclear'; fn.103 argues against reading it as primary stress (double occurrence in <chùpchùp>, and <yòro> marked on the Spanish-default penult). p.107: Juan & Ulloa 1748 'acento.. como de canto triste' quoted; Urban says interpretations from pitch accent/tone to intonation are all possible and 'moot'. p.110: regional Spanish words of possible Sechura origin often end in…

sources.citation: Urban, Matthias. 2015. El vocabulario sechurano de Richard Spruce. Lexis (PUCP) 39(2): 395-413.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: New transcription and facsimile of Spruce's 1864 Sechura wordlist (Kew). Discusses weakly articulated vowels (<kon'mpar> 'snake'; <cuctum> vs <cucatama> 'woman') and the Juan & Ulloa 'acento' remark; nothing on stress placement.
